summary:
[  edit  ]
The Lens Distort  TOP  applies or removes lens distortion from an image using the  Brown-Conrady model . This can be used to rectify images taken from a physical camera, to apply distortion to a rendering for use in augmented reality (AR), or as a visual effect.
The distortion algorithm used by the Lens Distort  TOP  can be broken down into three components: radial distortion, tangential distortion and the camera matrix.
Radial distortion shifts pixels in the output relative to their distance from the center of the image (defined by the Optical Center parameter). Radial distortion is controlled by the k1, k2 and k3 constants, with k1 having the greatest effect and k3 the least. Positive k values create a barrel or fisheye effect as if the image was wrapped around the surface of a sphere. Negative k values will bend the image inward to create a pincushion or pillow effect. The equations for radial distortion are:
x_distorted = x * (1 + k1 * r^2 + k2 * r^4 + k3 * r^6)
y_distorted = y * (1 + k1 * r^2 + k2 * r^4 + k3 * r^6)
where,
r = distance from center
Tangential distortion shifts pixels as if they were on a surface being tilted away from the camera and is controlled by the p1 and p2 parameters. p1 tilts the image up and down depending on the sign, and p2 tilts the image left and right. The equations for tangential distortion are:
x_distorted = x + (2 * p1 * x * y + p2 * (r^2 + 2 * x^2))
y_distorted = y + (p1 * (r^2 + 2 * y^2) + 2 * p2 * x * y)
where,
r = distance from center
The camera matrix is defined by the Optical Center and Focal Length parameters and is used to transform the image positions before the distortion is applied. The Optical Center values control where the center of the distortion effect is, while the Focal Length parameters act as a scale on the other effects. The camera matrix is usually represented as a 3x3 matrix:
fx   0    cx
0    fy   cy
0    0    1
Distortion values for a camera lens can be determined using  OpenCV calibration routines  or through functions for a particular camera (see  kinectazureTOP class ).
Barrel or Fisheye Radial Distortion, k > 0
Pillow or Pincushion Radial Distortion, k < 0
Tangential Distortion,   p1 < 0
Tangential Distortion,   p2 < 0
The  Layout  page has parameters to control how the distorted (or undistorted) image is arranged inside the output image frame. These features can be helpful to preserve parts of the input image that might otherwise be projected offscreen, to preserve input image resolution, or to establish a consistent output frame when lens distortion parameters are changing.
For example, setting the Post Transform parameter to Optimal and keeping Optimal Alpha at 1, the distorted image will be scaled and shifted so that the entire input image is kept within the output frame. Switching the  Layout  parameter to Native  Resolution , will then scale the output resolution so that no detail from the input image is lost. Attaching an  Info CHOP  will provide Region of Interest (ROI) bounds that can be used to crop out the original distorted image from the output image.
Note:  This  TOP  supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.label: Invert Distortion
parameters.name: invert
parameters.description: Reverse the lens distortion. This will *mostly* undo the distortion applied by another Lens Distort  TOP  with the same parameters and Inverse disabled.     The lens distortion algorithm does not have a precise inverse solution, so an approximate method is used which may not match the original image precisely. The quality of the approximation varies depending on the magnitude of the distortion. Additionally, the approximation aglorithm does not use the k3 constant and any content that was lost outside the bounds of the image cannot be recreated.

parameters.label: K1
parameters.name: k1
parameters.description: The first radial distortion constant. The k constants move pixels towards or away from the center of the image. Values greater than 0 produce a barrel or fisheye effect, while values less than zero produce a pillow or pincushion effect. k1 has a larger effect than k3.

parameters.label: K2
parameters.name: k2
parameters.description: The second radial distortion constant. See K1.

parameters.label: P1
parameters.name: p1
parameters.description: The first tangential distortion constant. Tilts the image up and down.

parameters.label: P2
parameters.name: p2
parameters.description: The second tangential distortion constant. Tilts the image left or right.

parameters.label: K3
parameters.name: k3
parameters.description: The third radial distortion constant (not used in the inverse distortion). See K1.

parameters.label: Optical Center
parameters.name: center
parameters.description: ⊞  - The position in the image that should be the center of the distortion. Depending on the unit mode selected, the position can be entered as an absolute position measured from the bottom-left corner, or as a relative position measured from the center of the image. The unit mode also controls whether the position is measured in pixels or normalized coordinates.

parameters.label: R
parameters.name: relative
parameters.description: The optical center is measured in normalized coordinates from -0.5 to -0.5 relative to the center of the image.

parameters.label: A
parameters.name: absolute
parameters.description: The optical center is measured in normalized coordinates (0 to 1) from the bottom-left corner of the image.

parameters.label: RP
parameters.name: pixelrel
parameters.description: The optical center is measured in pixel coordinates relative to the center of the image.

parameters.label: AP
parameters.name: pixelabs
parameters.description: The optical center is measured in absolute pixel coordinates from the bottom-left corner of the image.

parameters.label: Focal Lengths
parameters.name: focallength
parameters.description: ⊞  - The focal length components of the camera matrix descibed either as normalized resolution-independent values or as pixels. The focal length acts as a scalar on the other distortion parameters. The normalized unit mode can be used for systems that use millimeters or other physical units. Often abbreviated as Fx and Fy. See  OpenCV  for details.

parameters.label: F
parameters.name: fraction
parameters.description: The focal length is described in fractional or normalized coordinates.

parameters.label: P
parameters.name: pixels
parameters.description: The focal length is described in pixels.

parameters.label: Layout
parameters.name: layout
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the transformed image is arranged inside the final output image space. This value can be useful to preserve the native pixel resolution of the input image, or ensuring a final output resolution and aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Scale to Fit
parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: The transformed image is scaled to fill the full resolution and aspect ratio of the output image. This mode is useful if you want a specific output resolution or aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: native
parameters.description: The transformed image is arranged in the output in a way that preserves its original resolution and aspect ratio. This may mean the image is cropped if the output resolution is smaller than the input resolution.

parameters.label: Extend Mode
parameters.name: extendmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines what values are used when the output image exceeds the bounds of the input image.

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold
parameters.description: Colors from the outside edge of the input image are extended to fill any gaps in the output image.

parameters.label: Zero
parameters.name: zero
parameters.description: Empty gaps in the output image are filled with zeroes in all channels.

parameters.label: Repeat
parameters.name: repeat
parameters.description: The input image is tiled to fill gaps in the output image.

parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.name: mirror
parameters.description: The input image is mirrored and tiled to fill games in the output image.

parameters.label: Optimal Alpha
parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Determines how much of the image is preserved when calculating the optimal post transform. When zero, the optimal transform will include only the region of interest. When one, the transform will include all of the pixels from the input image. This value is equivalent to the 'alpha' value used in OpenCVs getOptimalNewCameraMatrix function.

parameters.label: Post Transform
parameters.name: transformmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose whether to preform an addition transformation to the image after the lens distortion is applied. This is useful for positioning and scaling the distorted image within the final image frame and can be used to preserve parts of the input image that would be shifted out of frame by the distortion.

parameters.label: None
parameters.name: none
parameters.description: No additional transformation is applied.

parameters.label: Optimal
parameters.name: optimal
parameters.description: The image is transformed according to the optimal new camera matrix as given by OpenCVs getOptimalNewCamera matrix. Depending on the value of the Optimal Alpha parameter, this mode can be used to ensure that none of the input image is lost outside of the image frame.

parameters.label: Custom
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Enables the custom center and scaling parameters. Use this option to modify the output image relative to the camera matrix on the Lens Distort page.

parameters.label: New Camera Matrix
parameters.name: newmatrix
parameters.description: Enter a new camera matrix for positioning the output image within the frame. Entering the camera matrix values from the Lens Distort page will result in no further transformation. Entering the optimal new camera matrix values will produce the same results as using the Optimal transform mode.

parameters.label: New Center
parameters.name: newcenter
parameters.description: ⊞  - A new optical center position that allows for shifting the transformed image within the output image frame. Using the same value as the Optical Center parameter will result in no post distortion offset. Using the Optimal Center value will produce the same results as the Optimal transform mode.

parameters.label: New Center Unit
parameters.name: newcenterunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the new center values are interpreted.

parameters.label: R
parameters.name: relative
parameters.description: The center is measured in normalized coordinates from -0.5 to -0.5 relative to the center of the image.

parameters.label: A
parameters.name: absolute
parameters.description: The center is measured in normalized coordinates (0 to 1) from the bottom-left corner of the image.

parameters.label: RP
parameters.name: pixelrel
parameters.description: The center is measured in pixel coordinates relative to the center of the image.

parameters.label: AP
parameters.name: pixelabs
parameters.description: The center is measured in absolute pixel coordinates from the bottom-left corner of the image.

parameters.label: New Focal Lengths
parameters.name: newfocallength
parameters.description: ⊞  - A new focal length that allows for scaling the transformed image relative to output image frame. Using the same value as the Focal Lengths parameter will result in no post distortion scaling. Using the Optimal Focal Length value will produce the same results as the Optimal transform mode.

parameters.label: F
parameters.name: fraction
parameters.description: The focal length is described in fractional or normalized coordinates.

parameters.label: P
parameters.name: pixels
parameters.description: The focal length is described in pixels.

parameters.label: Center Offset
parameters.name: centeroffset
parameters.description: ⊞  - Shifts the distorted image within the output image frame.

parameters.label: F
parameters.name: fraction
parameters.description: The offset amount is measured as a fraction of the output image from -0.5 to 0.5.

parameters.label: P
parameters.name: pixels
parameters.description: The offset amount is measured in pixels of the input image.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: ⊞  - Performs an additional post-distortion scale on the image. The scale is relative to the original camera matrix, so values greater than 1 will stretch the image, while values less than 1 will shrink it.

parameters.label: Cropping
parameters.name: cropmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Crop the transformed image so that only part of the image will appear in the final output. Unless a custom resolution is given, the cropped region will be used to determine the final output resolution.

parameters.label: None
parameters.name: none
parameters.description: No cropping is done.

parameters.label: Region of Interest
parameters.name: roi
parameters.description: The region of interest (ROI), as defined by the OpenCV function getNewCameraMatrix, is used to crop the final output. The ROI is automatically updated by any post transform functions, so this mode will still work when using a custom transform; however, cropping the ROI from a transformed image will generally produce the same result as using no transform or crop.

parameters.label: Custom
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Enter custom cropping region in pixels or as a fraction of the frame. Entering the ROI values from an attached Info  CHOP  will produce the same results as using the Region of Interest cropping mode.

parameters.label: Custom Region
parameters.name: cropregion
parameters.description: ⊞  - Defines a custom cropping region in the order of Left, Bottom, Right, Top. The values can either be as a fraction of the image (0-1) or as pixels of the input image size. Entering the ROI values from an attached Info  CHOP  will produce the same results as using the Region of Interest cropping mode.

parameters.label: Custom Region
parameters.name: cropregionx
parameters.description: The left side of the cropping region.

parameters.label: Custom Region
parameters.name: cropregiony
parameters.description: The bottom side of the cropping region.

parameters.label: Custom Region
parameters.name: cropregionz
parameters.description: The right side of the cropping region.

parameters.label: Custom Region
parameters.name: cropregionw
parameters.description: The top side of the cropping region.

parameters.label: Crop Unit
parameters.name: cropunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - The units used to interpret the values of the custom cropping region. Can be as fractions (0-1) of the image or as pixels of the input image size.

parameters.label: Scale Unit
parameters.name: scaleunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the scale values are used.

parameters.label: F
parameters.name: fraction
parameters.description: The scale is described in fractional or normalized coordinates.

parameters.label: P
parameters.name: pixels
parameters.description: The scale is described in pixels.

parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution.

parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.name: eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Half
parameters.name: half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 2X
parameters.name: 2x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 4X
parameters.name: 4x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 8X
parameters.name: 8x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Fits the width and height to the resolution given below, while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The width and height are limited to the resolution given below. If one of the dimensions exceeds the given resolution, the width and height will be reduced to fit inside the given limits while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Enables the  Resolution  parameter below, giving direct control over width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. Making this larger than 1 is essentially the same as taking the output from each pass, and passing it into the first input of the node and repeating the process. Other inputs and parameters remain the same for each pass.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue  Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono8fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16float
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono)
parameters.name: mono32float
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg8fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg16fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RG)
parameters.name: rg16float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RG)
parameters.name: rg32float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (A)
parameters.name: a8fixed
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 8-bits per channel, 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (A)
parameters.name: a16fixed
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (A)
parameters.name: a16float
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (A)
parameters.name: a32float
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 32-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha8fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha16fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha16float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha32float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: resy

parameters.label: aspectx

parameters.description: Depth of 2D or 3D array if this  TOP  contains a 2D or 3D texture array.

parameters.label: cook_time

parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.
